title: Retire (disable) the website and block access to all features

requirements.text: Add a canister-level "site retired" state that can be toggled by an administrator, and expose a public query to read the current site status (retired flag + optional public message).

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes a query method that returns whether the site is retired and a public-facing message.
Backend exposes an admin-only update method to set the site to retired (and optionally set/update the public message).
Non-admin callers cannot change the retired state (backend traps with an authorization error).

requirements.text: When the site is retired, block all non-admin, non-status backend operations (e.g., generation history mutations/queries and profile operations) so the application behaves as effectively deleted from the user perspective.

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: If the site is retired, non-admin calls to generation history APIs (get/add/update/delete) trap with a clear error message in English indicating the site is retired.
If the site is retired, non-admin calls to user profile APIs (get/save) trap with a clear error message in English indicating the site is retired.
Admin callers can still access admin-only operations while the site is retired (so an admin can manage/verify state).
The homepage content query continues to work (or is replaced by the site status query) without causing frontend crashes.

requirements.text: Add an admin-only backend operation to purge all stored user data (user profiles and generation history) to support “delete this website” as a data wipe, and make it available only when the site is retired.

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes an admin-only method that deletes all stored user profiles and all stored generation history records.
The purge method is rejected for non-admin callers.
The purge method is rejected unless the site is in retired state.
After purge, queries for profiles/history return empty results (or trap if retired per REQ-2), and no prior data remains accessible.

requirements.text: Implement a frontend "Site Retired" screen that replaces the normal app experience when the backend reports the site is retired, and ensure all routes (/, /text-to-image, /text-to-video, /text-to-voiceover, /my-history, /admin) render the retired screen for non-admin users.

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: When the backend indicates retired=true, navigating to any existing route shows a single retired page with a clear English message (using the backend-provided public message if present).
When retired=true, primary navigation and tool entry points are not shown to non-admin users.
The retired screen does not require authentication to view.
If the backend is not retired, the app behaves exactly as before.

requirements.text: Add an admin-only "Retire site" and "Purge all user data" control section to the existing Admin page, including a confirmation step to prevent accidental retirement/purge.

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: The Admin page shows controls to: (1) set the site to retired with an optional public message, and (2) purge all user data (only enabled/visible after retirement).
Both actions require an explicit confirmation (e.g., typing a confirmation phrase or a confirm dialog) before executing.
After successfully retiring the site, the UI reflects the new status without requiring a hard refresh.
Errors (e.g., non-admin, backend traps) are displayed to the admin in English via existing toast/error UI patterns.

requirements.text: Choose and apply a coherent visual theme for the "Site Retired" experience (typography, spacing, and neutral color palette) and use it consistently on the retired screen and admin retirement section.

quotes: I want to delete this website

acceptanceCriteria: The retired screen and admin retirement section share consistent styling (colors, typography, spacing).
No blue/purple-dominant palette is introduced unless already present; use a neutral/gray-based theme appropriate for a shutdown notice.
All user-facing text shown in these new UI surfaces is in English.

constraints: Do not modify files under frontend/src/components/ui (compose existing shadcn components instead).
Do not modify immutable hook/bootstrapping files listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts(x), frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx).
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo (no additional canisters/services).

This change cannot actually delete the canister or remove the URL from the Internet Computer; instead, implement a retired/disabled mode and (optionally) a data purge to achieve the practical effect of “deleting the website.”
nonGoals: Actual canister deletion, domain takedown, or removing the website from the network (not possible from within app code).
Adding third-party auth or external storage to archive/delete data.
Redesigning the existing non-retired app pages beyond what is necessary to gate them behind the retired mode.
